title: Self-work: watch CI on her own PR and fix red checks (#1398)
body:
Fixes #1398. Part of #1202.

After a self-work run ends `pr-open` or `pr-updated`, Mana watches that PR's CI: `gh pr checks <n>` every 60 s for up to 30 min.

- All green: the watch ends with a log line only.
- A red check: I read only the failing job's log tail (`gh run view --job <id> --log-failed`, last 3000 chars), scrubbed with sanitizeBridgeOutput and wrapped as untrusted, and run a refresh-style fix round (run kind `ci-fix`) on the same worktree and branch. It pushes through the existing refresh path, then the watch continues.
- At most 2 fix tries per PR number, then the run ends `needs-you` naming the failing check and what she tried.
- Gaming or RAM over the limit pauses the watch without counting. The open-PR limit part of `blocker()` is left out of the pause, since her own PR is open while she watches it (split into `resourceBlocker()`).
- Only one watch at a time; a new run or stop cancels it. Opt-in via `watchCi` (on in server.js). The watch and the tries are in memory like runs, so a backend restart drops them.

Tests (`node-bot/test/self-work-ci-watch.test.js`): fake gh and fake clock; green ends quietly, red then fixed, red twice then needs-you, gaming pauses, stop cancels.
interface: The merged change for PR #1403 is covered by test/self-work-ci-watch.test.js.
why: Additional real merged-fix benchmark case selected to broaden the agentic coding evaluation.
